$comment: Change-impact contract for grouped-nf4-gemm: which companion changes a class of change requires before it is complete. scripts/check_change_impact.py --base <git ref> detects the triggers it can see in a diff and reports the missing companions (FAIL or WARN as listed); the steps a script cannot see are the human checklist. docs/system-manifest.json names the invariants this contract serves (kernel-first, claims-own-numbers, status-owns-position). Human-readable summary: AGENTS.md section 8.
checked_by: scripts/check_change_impact.py --base <git ref> (CI runs it on pull requests against the PR base)

classes.description: A new kernel or primitive that a consumer can call: a new module in pyproject py-modules, or a new @triton.jit kernel in a shipped module.
detected_triggers: a module added to [tool.setuptools] py-modules in pyproject.toml
a new @triton.jit-decorated function in a module pyproject ships
a module-level layout constant (BLOCK / GROUP / STRIDE / ALIGN / LAYOUT / NIBBLE / PACK / ROW / TILE / WIDTH / BYTES) added or changed in a shipped module

warn_if_missing: docs/KERNEL_CONTRACT.md (only when a layout constant changed)

steps.what: kernel implementation and its pure-torch reference
steps.where: kernel/<module>.py: the kernel, and a reference the tests assert it against

steps.what: kernel contract / layout documentation
steps.where: docs/KERNEL_CONTRACT.md (layouts at a glance; the op contract) and the module docstring

steps.what: capability entry
steps.where: docs/capabilities.json: an entry (or an entrypoint on an existing entry) with status, limitations and claim_ids; scripts/check_capabilities.py validates it

steps.what: kernel tests wired into CI
steps.where: kernel/test_<module>.py named in .github/workflows/ci.yml (kernel/test_packaging_covers_kernel.py enforces it); interpreter-mode files registered in kernel/conftest.py _INTERP_FILES

steps.what: consumer integration
steps.where: experts4bit-qlora: the enable_* path that calls the kernel and returns a count or handle (no silent fallback)

steps.what: consumer floor, if the consumer requires the new kernel
steps.where: after the kernel release is tagged: experts4bit-qlora pyproject `fast` extra and a new compatibility record in docs/system-manifest.json, byte-identical in both repositories (kernel-first invariant; scripts/check_system_manifest.py)

steps.what: model-level measurement
steps.where: experts4bit-qlora receipts (kernel-level cells stay here under kernel/ or bench/)

steps.what: quality gate
steps.where: the registered gate in its own units, verdict recorded as PASS or FAIL beside a measured noise floor; a failed gate stays failed

steps.what: claim registration
steps.where: docs/claims.json in the repository that owns the number (kernel-level here, model-level in the consumer); docs/STATUS.md in the same change; prose quotes the claim ID

steps.what: release documentation
steps.where: CHANGELOG.md under the release that ships it (first paragraph per docs/RELEASE_NOTES_GUIDE.md); llms-full.txt regenerated (scripts/build_llms_bundle.py)

classes.description: A public kernel, reference or primitive changes signature, layout or return, or an entry point is added to or removed from the capability contract.
detected_triggers: the set of entrypoints in docs/capabilities.json changes

steps.what: module docstring and docs/KERNEL_CONTRACT.md if a layout moved
README entry-point table, docs/capabilities.json entrypoints, the affected docs/solutions/*.md
CHANGELOG.md under ## Unreleased
the consumer-side change or issue in experts4bit-qlora

classes.description: A number changes or appears: a receipt, then the claim, then the position, then prose that quotes the claim ID. docs/claims.json wins for numbers; docs/STATUS.md wins for position.
detected_triggers: a claim added to docs/claims.json, or an existing claim's status, value or unit changed

steps.what: receipt committed (public path under evidence) or labelled measured-private with evidence_private
claim entry in docs/claims.json with status from the evidence vocabulary; a superseded or retired claim keeps its entry and names its successor or reason
docs/STATUS.md states the new position (what it does today / what changed / what is open)
prose quotes the claim ID and tier (README, solution pages, capabilities.json limitations); numbers with units never enter docs/capabilities.json
llms-full.txt regenerated

classes.description: The package version, a dependency floor (torch, triton, numpy) or the consumer's floor on this package changes.

warn_if_missing: README.md and docs/capabilities.json environments (on a dependency-floor change)

steps.what: version bump: CHANGELOG.md carries the release heading; the tag is cut by the maintainer after merge (publish.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with pyproject)
dependency floor: the pyproject comment records why; README install note and docs/capabilities.json environments follow; scripts/check_dependency_floor.py validates the hand-copied floors

consumer floor: only after the kernel release exists -- a new compatibility record in docs/system-manifest.json in BOTH repositories and the consumer's `fast` extra; scripts/check_system_manifest.py --sibling checks the pair
